text:
ash: Heads up — saw a steady memory growth on long-context requests on Dedicated that doesn't show up on Hosted. Repro with 64k tokens, long chat sessions.
kevin: hmm, is this the kv cache leak we've seen before or different?
maria: can you paste the profiler output? :thinking:
ash: attaching quick flame summary (trimmed):
```
KV cache resident: hosted 18GB, dedicated 34GB, private 29GB
page_faults/sec: dedicated 420, hosted 25
evict_count: dedicated 12M, hosted 400k
avg_page_size: 16KB
kernel: fallback->attn_slow when seq>8k
```
kevin: fallback to attn_slow explains CPU spike but why paging difference? Dedicated config uses KV_PAGE_SIZE=16k vs hosted 64k?
maria: right — on Dedicated we had tuned for smaller pages for memory packing, but that increases metadata and fragmentation. Private onprem default is 32k.
liam: also check MTU on VPC for Private — we've seen reassemblies causing extra kernel copies which look like fragmentation in the allocator.
ash: confirmed: dedicated machines are on AWS with ENA v2, mtu 9001, but the customer's VPC had mtu 1500 and path MTU inconsistent for Private tests. That mismatch caused extra syscalls and higher page faults.
kevin: oof. Is jemalloc vs tcmalloc different across builds? That can change slab behavior and evict patterns.
maria: Dedicated AMI uses jemalloc 5.3, Hosted container image is using mimalloc. I think jemalloc's extents cause more split/merge churn under lots of small allocations (kv frames).
liam: action: reproduce with identical kernel/userland and just swap allocator to isolate. Also run with KV_PAGER_DEBUG=1 to capture eviction traces.
nash: ran quick patch: forced mimalloc on Dedicated -> resident dropped ~6GB after warmup, evict_count down 7x. Still seeing occasional kernel fallback at 8k which slows throughput.
kevin: what's causing kernel selection to fallback? We had a regressed kernel selector after the recent runtime change to support grouped attention. It picks a slower kernel when sequence distribution has heavy tail.
maria: yes, profiler shows selector picks attn_grouped when avg_seq<2k but then when tails hit 8k it fails compatibility check and falls back to attn_slow. Need to update the compatibility mask and add better cost heuristics.
liam: could batching heuristics help? If we split the request into smaller micro-batches we avoid huge KV frames. But that impacts latency SLO.
nash: tried micro-batching (batch size 4 -> 8) reduced peak resident but increased median latency by ~12ms. For Dedicated customers with throughput SLAs that might be ok if we provide config knob.
kevin: another angle: kv pager eviction policy. Currently we evict LRU frames aggressively when pressure > threshold. But fragmentation causes many small free spans that are unusable; compaction would help but is expensive.
maria: compiled a quick config diff we should try on Dedicated:
```
KV_PAGE_SIZE=32768
KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.78
KV_COMPACT_INTERVAL=600
KV_BATCH_PADDING=128
```
These reduced fragmentation in local tests.
liam: for Hosted we keep page size big to minimize metadata, but we also run a kernel with strong contiguous allocation guarantees (hugepages enabled). That explains hosted's stability.
sre-bot: deploy scheduled: eng-runtime/kv-compact-experiment -> staging at 2024-06-05T18:00:00Z
kevin: plan: 1) run allocator swap test (jemalloc->mimalloc) on Dedicated 2) apply KV_PAGE_SIZE=32k and run 64k token soak for 12h 3) add selector heuristics to avoid attn_grouped fallback on heavy-tail sequences 4) evaluate micro-batching tradeoffs and expose knob to customers
maria: I'll own steps 1+2. Nash+Li am pair on 3. Put results in the perf doc and link to rollout playbook.
nash: quick repro script I used:
```
# run long-context generator
python tools/long_chat.py --model redwood/xxl --tokens 65536 --concurrency 2 --duration 4h
# enable debug
export KV_PAGER_DEBUG=1
export MALLOC_CONF=stats_print:true
```
kevin: thanks. Also let's capture kernelperf traces and profile with per-request kv_usage histogram. That should show how much of the cost is syscall/page-fault vs CPU kernels.
liam: noted. I'll also add an A/B in Dedicated: current vs compacting pager with background compaction disabled during peak windows to avoid CPU interference.
maria: if this fixes Dedicated we'll propose default config aligned with Hosted to reduce surprises for customers migrating between modes.
nash: one more gotcha: onprem customers with older GPU drivers (470.x) had different mmap alignment which forced 4k pages — that's a killer. We should add a compatibility check in the installer and recommend driver >= 515 and hugepage support.
kevin: agreed. Add that to Private onboarding checklist.
nash: thanks y'all. I'll post the raw traces and a short summary in the perf board after the staging run. :thumbsup:
kevin: glory to reproducible perf. :party_popper:
